Who Has Been Asked, and Where Are the Notes?

The conversations behind this decision on one page: who has been asked, when, where the notes are, and who is still to hear from.

Download PDF

Your loved one told you something important in the car last week. Your sister put her view in a long text. Your uncle said his piece on the phone, and nobody wrote it down.

This page doesn't ask you to weigh any of it. It asks who has been asked, on what day, where the notes are, and who is holding them.

What to collectDate asked or writtenWhere the notes areWho has them
What your loved one has said they want, in their own words
What they've said about a good day, and the routines and choices they want to keep
Things they said in earlier conversations that someone remembers but hasn't written down
One relative's concerns and hoped-for outcome. Name: ________
Another relative's concerns and hoped-for outcome. Name: ________
Another relative's concerns and hoped-for outcome. Name: ________
What each relative has said they can and cannot realistically do
Where the family agrees, as far as it's been written down
Where expectations conflict, as far as it's been written down
Questions that need a doctor, a nurse or another professional, and who is taking each one

Scroll sideways to see every column, or print this page to fill it in.

Who hasn't been asked yet, and who will ask

Anyone involved in the decision who has no line above, and any line above with nothing beside it. Put a name next to each.

For example Aunt Rose hasn't been asked. Marcus will phone her on Thursday. The conversation in the car last week isn't written down. I'll do that tonight.

How to use it

  • Write the day each person was asked. A view passed along by someone else goes down as “not asked yet.”
  • Don't summarize or tidy anyone's answer here. Just say where it is.
  • Your loved one's lines come first on the page. If they're empty, that's the first conversation to have.
  • Bring this page, and the notes it points to, to the family conversation.

What this page doesn't do

It doesn't weigh anyone's answer, say whose view counts for more, or explain what anyone meant. It shows who has been heard and where their words are kept.
